newsitem.title: JAPAN: N'tendo to site software machines at 24-hr stores.
newsitem.headline: N'tendo to site software machines at 24-hr stores.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Thursday that it plans from the summer of 1997 to site machines at convenience stores in Japan that will enable customers to download its game software.
The company has agreed with convenience store operator Lawson Inc to sell game software for Nintendo's Super Famicom game console under the distribution scheme, a Nintendo spokesman said.

Under the scheme, consumers will be able to download software titles of their choice on a cassette, which will be sold for about 5,000 yen, from machines installed in Lawson stores, Nintendo said in a statement.
Prices for down-loading one game title will likely range from 1,000 to 4,000 yen, the statement said.
Lawson operates nearly 6,000 convenience stores throughout Japan and is a group firm of Daiei Inc, Japan's leading supermarket operator.
